name: Credentials from Web Browsers

evidence.rationale: Remote wipe of managed browser profiles can remove locally stored enterprise passwords and related authentication data. Browser-synchronized credentials and already extracted copies require separate account or server-side action.
Inactive accounts may be targeted by attackers to gain unauthorized access. Disabling inactive accounts can prevent attackers from acquiring credentials from web browsers.

Automated browser updates remove known vulnerabilities that could expose stored passwords, tokens, or browser authentication data. Patching does not prevent credential theft by malware already executing with sufficient access to the browser profile.

Correcting identified browser vulnerabilities reduces exploit-based extraction of stored passwords, tokens, and other authentication data. This does not prevent theft by malware that already has sufficient access to the browser profile.

Current browser versions reduce exploitation of known weaknesses that expose stored passwords and authentication data. Updating the browser does not prevent credential theft by malware already executing with access to the user's browser profile.

Malicious extensions may access credentials stored in browsers. Extension restrictions reduce that attack surface, but malware already executing with access to the browser profile may still extract stored credentials.
Web filtering and application-layer gateways can block malicious web content and destinations used to deliver browser-based credential theft or session-stealing content.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.
